chunks: And with this chain of narrators, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Muhammad ibn al-Fadl, from Abu Hamza, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: You are for Paradise and Paradise is yours. Your names with us are the Virtuous and the Reformers. You are the people of contentment with Allah, for He is pleased with you. The angels are your brothers in virtue if they strive diligently.
ai.seo_question: What is the status of the virtuous believers in relation to Paradise and the angels according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Fadail al-Shia, Imam al-Sadi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the ontological bond between the faithful and Paradise, describing them as 'the people of mutual contentment' (Ahl al-Rida) with Allah. This reciprocal satisfaction highlights the Shia concept of divine love and human striving, where angels are depicted as spiritual siblings in virtue, emphasizing the community's collective moral excellence and readiness for the afterlife.
